questions.stem: Which legislation specifically addresses the scope of practice, authorized acts, and title protection for medical radiation technologists in Ontario?
options: The Regulated Health Professions Act, 1991 alone
The Nuclear Safety and Control Act
The Health Protection and Promotion Act
The Medical Radiation Technologists Act, 2017
questions.explanation: The MRIT Act, 2017 sets out the scope, authorized acts, and protected title for medical radiation technologists, including sonographers.

questions.stem: Which of the following is one of the five authorized acts that CMRITO registrants are authorized to perform?
options: Performing surgery under general anaesthesia
Performing a procedure on tissue below the dermis
Prescribing controlled substances
Performing open-heart surgery
questions.explanation: The five authorized acts include procedures on tissue below the dermis, among others listed in the legislation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the five authorized acts for CMRITO registrants?
options: The injection or inhalation of substances
Tracheal suctioning of a tracheostomy
Applying energy prescribed by a physician
The application of sound waves for diagnostic ultrasound
questions.explanation: Applying sound waves for diagnostic ultrasound is permitted under an RHPA exemption, not as one of the five authorized acts.

questions.stem: In an echocardiography laboratory, a sonographer instills agitated saline or an ultrasound-enhancing agent. Which category does this fall under?
options: The injection of substances
Tracheal suctioning
X-ray production
Nuclear medicine imaging
questions.explanation: Introducing agitated saline or an enhancing agent into the circulation constitutes injection of a substance.

questions.stem: A sonographer starts an intravenous line. Which authorized act does this involve?
options: The inhalation of substances
Tracheal suctioning
A procedure on tissue below the dermis
The application of prescribed energy
questions.explanation: Inserting an IV involves penetrating tissue below the skin surface — a procedure on tissue below the dermis.

questions.stem: Which legislation governs x-ray imaging and the X-Ray Safety Code?
options: The Nuclear Safety and Control Act
The Medical Radiation Technologists Act, 2017 alone
The Environmental Protection Act
The Radiation Emitting Devices Act and associated x-ray safety provisions under the RHPA framework
questions.explanation: X-ray safety is governed by federal radiation-emitting device legislation and provincial x-ray safety provisions — not by the sonography scope.

questions.stem: Under which legislation do nuclear medicine and radiation therapy fall?
options: The Regulated Health Professions Act exemption for ultrasound
The Nuclear Safety and Control Act, as applied to those specific professions
The Residential Tenancies Act
The Motor Vehicle Act
questions.explanation: Nuclear medicine and radiation therapy activities are addressed under nuclear safety legislation, distinct from ultrasound practice.

questions.stem: What is a "controlled act"?
options: Any activity performed in a hospital
Any task that a sonographer finds difficult
A task that requires no training
An activity listed in legislation that may only be performed by authorized members of specified professions
questions.explanation: Controlled acts are restricted by law to specific authorized professionals to protect the public.

questions.stem: Why can an Ontario sonographer perform diagnostic ultrasound even though ultrasound application is not listed among the five authorized acts?
options: Because the RHPA specifically exempts applying sound waves for diagnostic ultrasound
Because anyone may perform ultrasound without restriction
Because hospitals can override legislation
Because the sonographer's employer grants the authority alone
questions.explanation: The exemption in the RHPA permits the application of sound waves for diagnostic ultrasound by those within the profession's scope.

questions.stem: A sonographer performs tracheal suctioning of a tracheostomy. How is this activity classified?
options: As an unrestricted activity anyone may perform
As an activity reserved exclusively for dentists
As one of the five authorized acts available to CMRITO registrants
As an x-ray procedure
questions.explanation: Tracheal suctioning of a tracheostomy is explicitly included among the five authorized acts.

questions.stem: Which pairing of legislation and subject is CORRECT?
options: Nuclear Safety and Control Act — diagnostic ultrasound scope in Ontario
RHPA, 1991 — hospital parking regulations
NSC Act — regulating sonographers' professional conduct
MRIT Act, 2017 — scope, authorized acts, and title protection for medical radiation technologists
questions.explanation: The MRIT Act, 2017 correctly governs scope, authorized acts, and title protection for this group.

questions.stem: A sonographer is consistently late for shifts, causing colleagues to cover their patients. Which professional behaviour is being violated?
options: Image optimization
Informed consent
Scope of practice
Reliability and responsibility to the team
questions.explanation: Reliability is a core professional behaviour; chronic lateness burdens colleagues and disrupts patient care.

questions.stem: Which action best reflects professionalism in appearance and identification?
options: Wearing the required identification and adhering to the dress code
Wearing whatever is most comfortable regardless of policy
Removing identification to avoid patient questions
Dressing to attract attention
questions.explanation: Proper identification and dress support trust, safety, and recognition within the care team.

questions.stem: Why is hand hygiene essential between patients?
options: It is only a suggestion, not a standard
It prevents healthcare-associated infection transmission
It saves time
It improves image quality
questions.explanation: Hand hygiene is a foundational infection prevention practice that protects patients and staff.

questions.stem: A sonographer must examine a sensitive area. Which approach best reflects professionalism?
options: Explain the need, obtain ongoing consent, and use draping to preserve dignity
Expose as much as possible for speed
Skip the area entirely without telling anyone
Allow bystanders to observe for teaching without consent
questions.explanation: Explanation, ongoing consent, and draping preserve patient dignity while allowing necessary imaging.

questions.stem: A patient requests that a same-gender sonographer perform the examination if possible. What is the most professional response?
options: Dismiss the request as unreasonable
Refuse the examination entirely
Ignore the request
Respect the request where feasible, accommodate it when possible, and document the arrangement
questions.explanation: Respecting patient preferences regarding modesty and culture, when feasible, reflects patient-centred professionalism.

questions.stem: A patient becomes hostile and insulting during an examination. What is the best response?
options: Respond with equal hostility
Walk out and abandon the patient
Post about the patient online
Remain calm, de-escalate, continue to provide safe care, and involve a supervisor if needed
questions.explanation: Maintaining composure, de-escalating, and escalating appropriately protects both the patient and the professional.

questions.stem: Two colleagues are in a heated argument in the ultrasound department with patients nearby. What should a professionalism-focused employee do?
options: Record the argument for entertainment
Address or report the disruption so patient care and dignity are protected
Ignore it completely regardless of patient impact
Take sides loudly
questions.explanation: Unprofessional conflict in a clinical area must be managed to protect patients and the care environment.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an unacceptable use of social media by a sonographer?
options: Sharing general health education content approved by the workplace
Attending a professional webinar announced online
Networking with colleagues
Posting identifiable patient information or images
questions.explanation: Posting identifiable patient information is a serious confidentiality breach and professional misconduct.

questions.stem: A sonographer is extremely fatigued after several night shifts and is about to start a complex study. What is the most professional action?
options: Push through without telling anyone
Disclose the fatigue concern to a supervisor so patient safety can be protected
Speed up the examination regardless of accuracy
Ask the patient to reschedule without explanation
questions.explanation: Fatigue impairs performance; disclosing it and seeking mitigation is a patient-safety obligation.

questions.stem: A sonographer notices a medication error being prepared for a patient by another staff member. What is the appropriate action?
options: Say nothing to avoid conflict
Wait to see whether harm occurs
Intervene or report the unsafe practice immediately to protect the patient
Post a complaint on social media
questions.explanation: Patient safety takes precedence; unsafe practices must be raised immediately through appropriate channels.

questions.stem: Why is continuing professional development a professional responsibility?
options: It maintains and enhances competence throughout a career
It is required only for new graduates
It is optional and unrelated to practice
It replaces workplace orientation
questions.explanation: Knowledge and technology evolve; ongoing development keeps competence current.

questions.stem: Which behaviour best demonstrates interprofessional respect?
options: Dismissing input from nurses and other team members
Communicating courteously and collaborating with all members of the care team
Working in complete isolation from the team
Publicly criticizing colleagues to patients
questions.explanation: Respectful, collaborative communication with all professions supports safe and effective care.

questions.stem: A patient is nervous and asks repeated questions about the examination. Which response best reflects patient-centred care?
options: Answer respectfully, provide clear explanations, and check the patient's understanding
Tell the patient to stop asking and lie still
Complete the examination as fast as possible without responding
Ask the patient's family to answer instead
questions.explanation: Patient-centred care involves attentive communication, clear explanation, and confirmation of understanding.

questions.stem: A sonographer realizes they omitted a required image series from a completed study. What is the most professional response?
options: Hide the omission and hope it is not noticed
Blame the patient for moving
Acknowledge the error, correct it (including re-acquiring images if possible), and document transparently
Delete the study entirely
questions.explanation: Honesty about errors, prompt correction, and transparent documentation are hallmarks of professional integrity.

questions.stem: A patient tries to share personal gifts or excessive favour with the sonographer. What is the appropriate professional response?
options: Accept anything offered without question
Post about the gift on social media
Maintain professional boundaries, decline appropriately, and keep the relationship professional
Use the gift to influence examination quality
questions.explanation: Maintaining appropriate boundaries protects both the patient and the professional relationship.

questions.stem: A sonographer is running behind schedule but notices that the required images for the current study are incomplete. What should take priority?
options: Completing the required images properly and communicating the delay
Cutting corners to save time
Skipping documentation entirely
Leaving the study unfinished without telling anyone
questions.explanation: Examination completeness and honest communication take priority over schedule pressure.

questions.stem: A physician asks a sonographer to change a technical impression to something the images do not support. What is the correct response?
options: Comply without question because the physician is senior
Decline to alter objective findings and escalate the concern through appropriate channels
Alter the report quietly and say nothing
Delete the original images
questions.explanation: Objectivity and honesty in documentation cannot be compromised; the sonographer must escalate rather than falsify findings.

questions.stem: A staff member is being harassed by a colleague. What is the appropriate professional response?
options: Ignore it indefinitely
Retaliate privately
Discuss it with patients
Report it through the workplace's established channels and support a respectful environment
questions.explanation: Harassment must be reported through formal channels to protect staff and maintain a professional workplace.

questions.stem: The department introduces a new ultrasound system. What should a sonographer do before using it on patients?
options: Use it immediately without training
Ask patients to figure it out
Complete the required training and demonstrate competence first
Avoid the system permanently
questions.explanation: New technology requires orientation, training, and competency validation before clinical use.

questions.stem: What is evidence-based practice in sonography?
options: Integrating current best evidence, clinical expertise, and patient values in practice decisions
Using the newest equipment regardless of outcomes
Following only personal tradition
Doing whatever is fastest
questions.explanation: Evidence-based practice combines the best available evidence with professional judgement and patient preferences.

questions.stem: What is the value of reflective practice for a sonographer?
options: It has no value once one is experienced
It replaces supervision
It encourages self-assessment, identification of learning needs, and continuous improvement
It is only required for students
questions.explanation: Reflection drives ongoing professional growth by identifying strengths and areas needing development.

questions.stem: A patient cannot afford a follow-up examination they clearly need. What is the sonographer's most appropriate role?
options: Ignore the issue entirely
Promise the examination for free personally
Tell the patient it is not the sonographer's concern
Advocate within the care team and connect the patient with appropriate resources or social work
questions.explanation: Advocacy within the team and connection to resources supports equitable, patient-centred care.

questions.stem: A patient collapses in the department during an examination. Which sequence best reflects professional emergency behaviour?
options: Continue the examination to complete the images first
Leave the room to avoid responsibility
Wait for the patient to recover on their own
Stop the examination, call for emergency assistance, provide appropriate support, and document the event
questions.explanation: Patient safety comes first: stop, call for help, assist within competence, and document the event fully.

questions.stem: A sonographer is experiencing personal stress that begins affecting concentration at work. What is the most professional course of action?
options: Ignore it and pretend everything is fine
Take it out on patients
Seek appropriate support and inform a supervisor so patient safety is not compromised
Resign immediately without notice
questions.explanation: Recognizing impairment to practice and seeking support protects both the practitioner and patients.

questions.stem: Which combination of actions BEST represents overall professional practice in the Week 1 context?
options: Completing as many examinations as possible with minimal documentation
Following orders without question and never communicating with the care team
Prioritizing personal convenience over patient preparation
Verifying the order, assessing the patient, working within scope and competence, documenting objectively, and escalating concerns promptly
questions.explanation: Professional practice integrates order verification, patient assessment, scope and competence, accurate documentation, and timely communication and escalation.
